name: Hair transplant (FUE/FUT)

card.summary: Surgical relocation of follicles from the back of the scalp to thinning or bald areas; an established, durable procedure that depends on donor supply and surgeon skill.
card.aka: hair restoration surgery, follicular unit extraction, follicular unit transplantation, strip surgery, Turkey hair transplant
card.note: Transplanted hair does not stop native hair loss from continuing, and quality varies widely between clinics.
card.price: Roughly $1-7 per graft depending on country, per Wikipedia

quick.overview:
A hair transplant moves hair follicles from a donor area, usually the back and sides of the scalp, into areas of thinning or baldness. The two main harvesting methods are follicular unit transplantation (FUT, or strip surgery) and follicular unit extraction (FUE), in which individual follicular units are taken with small punches.

Medical literature describes it as a well-established treatment for androgenetic alopecia and some other conditions, based on the principle of donor dominance. Looksmaxxing forums discuss it heavily, including trips to clinics in Turkey for lower prices, and members disagree about how reliable results are.
quick.mechanism: Hair follicles from the donor area are genetically resistant to the hormone-driven miniaturization of pattern baldness and tend to keep that behavior after relocation, which is called donor dominance. FUT removes a strip of scalp that is dissected into grafts; FUE removes units one at a time. Grafts are placed in tiny recipient sites, where they shed and regrow over months.
quick.risks: Reported effects include swelling, itching, temporary numbness, scarring at the donor area, temporary shedding of the transplanted hair, folliculitis and infection. Native hair around transplanted areas can continue to thin, so surgeons often combine surgery with medical therapy. Quality and safety vary by clinic, and forum posts describe poor outcomes as well as good ones.

lead: Hair transplantation is a surgical procedure in which hair follicles from a donor region, typically the back and sides of the scalp, are relocated to areas of hair loss [1][2]. It is used mainly for androgenetic alopecia (male and female pattern hair loss), and also for some scarring alopecias and to correct trauma or prior surgery [2][3]. Modern practice is built on follicular unit transplantation, in which naturally occurring groups of one to four hairs are used as grafts [2].

The two main ways of obtaining grafts are follicular unit transplantation from a harvested strip (FUT, strip surgery) and follicular unit extraction (FUE), in which individual units are removed with small punches. FUE was described in a 2002 paper and has since been joined by robotic systems [4][1][5]. A 2025 review concluded that both FUE and strip excision are state-of-the-art methods and that hair transplantation has grown in popularity because of advances in devices, techniques and medical therapies that maintain density [6].

Hair transplantation has become one of the most discussed procedures in looksmaxxing communities, including clinic tourism to Turkey, where Wikipedia reports prices as low as about 1 US dollar per graft compared with several times that in some Western countries [1]. Forum members debate candidacy, hairline design and the reliability of advertised success rates [7][8].

paras: FUT (strip harvesting) removes a strip of scalp from the back of the head, which is dissected under magnification into follicular units. It leaves a thin linear scar that is usually concealed by hair, and Wikipedia gives recovery as about two weeks [1]. FUE removes individual follicular units with punches of roughly 0.6 to 1.0 millimeters, leaving small scattered scars, and recovery is under a week, although sessions take longer and cost more [1].

The original description of FUE in 2002 introduced it as an alternative for patients concerned about strip scarring [4]. Robotic hair transplantation allows precise removal of follicular units and is considered a tool that does not replace candidate selection, hairline design and surgeon judgment [9]. A randomized study of 24 patients examined robotic graft selection based on hair number per unit [10]. A randomized trial studied de-epithelialization of grafts and graft survival after FUE [11]. Variants such as direct hair implantation (DHI) with an implanter pen are described in Grokipedia, which is not fully reliable [12].

A Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology review describes anatomical concepts and guidelines for choosing good and bad candidates, noting that not all hair disorders are suitable for transplantation [2]. The Norwood classification of male pattern baldness, first published in 1975, is commonly used to describe the extent of loss [13]. A 2023 review notes that for pediatric androgenetic alopecia there is no approved therapy and hair transplant may be an option for girls in selected cases [14]. Reviews state that thoughtful hairline design and concurrent medical management improve aesthetic results [6].

A 2024 systematic review of 141 studies on androgenetic alopecia found that procedural treatments including hair transplantation promote hair growth and emphasized a multifaceted, individualized approach [15]. A 2025 review reports long-lasting, natural results and high patient satisfaction with current techniques [6]. Grokipedia gives graft survival as 85 to 95 percent and full results at 12 to 18 months, but also lists inconsistent satisfaction figures within the same article, so these numbers are not treated as established [12].

Because transplanted hair keeps its genetic properties in the new location (donor dominance), it is generally expected to persist, while native hair near the recipient area can continue to thin [6]. Reviews recommend concurrent medical management to maintain density [6].

Wikipedia describes temporary shedding of transplanted hair (shock loss) as common and notes that post-operative antibiotics are often prescribed [1]. Other reported effects include swelling, itching, numbness and scarring, with folliculitis and infection less common, according to Grokipedia [12]. Wikipedia also notes that alcohol and smoking are said to reduce graft survival [1]. A randomized trial studied hair follicle microtissue for promoting wound healing and alleviating complications after transplantation [16].

Wikipedia gives an average cost per graft ranging from about 1.07 US dollars in Turkey to 7 dollars in Canada, and notes that some clinics sell all-inclusive packages [1]. Grokipedia gives sessions in Turkey as costing roughly 2,500 to 5,000 dollars compared with 10,000 to 20,000 in the US, but this is an AI-generated source [12]. Looksmax.org members report traveling to Turkey for hair transplants combined with other surgeries, and describe being targeted by lead-generation messages from clinics after a procedure [17][18].

Forum threads ask about effectiveness, timing (for example, at 19 or wait until 25), small-area transplants and how surgeons judge a case [8][19][20][21]. In one thread a poster argues that advertised success rates above 95 percent are inflated and that results depend on ideal characteristics such as low Norwood grade and dense donor hair, citing an acquaintance who works with top surgeons [8]. Others share surgeon opinions on their own cases and a long guide thread [21][22]. Some members present hair transplants as one step among several surgeries, such as rhinoplasty, bimaxillary surgery, blepharoplasty and fat transfer [23].

Trials in the literature include a randomized bilateral study of robotic follicular unit graft selection in 24 patients [10], a randomized trial of de-epithelialization before graft insertion after FUE [11], and a randomized trial of hair follicle microtissue after transplantation [16]. A trial of stromal vascular fraction-enriched platelet-rich plasma in androgenetic alopecia has also been published [24]. Registered studies include platelet-rich plasma versus nanofat as adjuncts to transplantation, fat grafting in scleroderma-related alopecia, and hair transplantation in cicatricial alopecia [25][26][27].
The 2024 systematic review and 2025 state-of-the-art review summarize the broader evidence for transplantation as part of androgenetic alopecia care [15][6].

timeline.event: Menahem Hodara moves hair from healthy scalp to scars on bald areas, per Wikipedia [1].
Japanese surgeon Okuda reports small hair grafts used mainly for eyebrows and lashes [1].
Norman Orentreich begins using donor grafts for male pattern baldness and shows donor dominance [1].
Norwood classification of male pattern baldness is published [13].
Follicular unit extraction (FUE) is described in Dermatologic Surgery [4].
NeoGraft robotic device receives FDA approval; ARTAS follows in 2011 [1].

lore.intro: Hair transplants are among the most discussed surgeries on looksmax.org, often paired with questions about medical hair-loss treatment, hairline design, Turkey clinics and results shared in before-and-after posts [8][19][23].

claims.claim: Transplant success rates above 95 percent are overstated and results are a gamble.
claims.believers: One poster argues advertised success rates are inflated and that outcomes are unpredictable even with top specialists, and that the procedure is only worth it with ideal characteristics such as low Norwood grade and dense donor hair [8].
claims.experts: Reviews report long-lasting natural results and high satisfaction with modern techniques but stress candidate selection, hairline design and concurrent medical therapy [6][2].

claims.claim: Hair transplant is a good last-resort option for someone who expects to go bald young.
claims.believers: Posters ask whether transplantation works as a last resort for early genetic hair loss and share surgeon feedback [8][21].
claims.experts: A systematic review lists hair transplantation among procedural treatments that promote hair growth in androgenetic alopecia, and a 2025 review says that concurrent medical management helps maintain density [15][6].

claims.claim: Turkey clinics offer comparable results at much lower prices.
claims.believers: Members report flying to Turkey for hair transplantation combined with other operations and discuss lower prices [17][23].
claims.experts: Wikipedia gives Turkey as the lowest-priced location per graft; the sources reviewed do not compare outcomes between countries [1].

claims.claim: Timing matters: getting a transplant very young may cause problems as loss progresses.
claims.believers: A thread asks whether to get a transplant at 19 or wait until 25, and another poster says it can be too late if treatment is delayed [19].
claims.experts: Reviews emphasize candidate selection and concurrent medical management to maintain density as loss progresses [6][2].
